artifact: Surface v12 SaaS V1 corrected structured reconstruction
conclusion: The corrected SaaS and control artifacts use one fixed generic host, have complete reasoning traces, pass all seven graph phases, and pass the four required technical outcome cases without product-specific host code. The aggregate demo claim remains held for human adequacy approval.

construction.note: The corrected artifacts were reconstructed directly after closing authoring, validation, trace, and host-boundary gaps. Attempt 7 remains historical failed public-builder evidence.

disqualifying_findings.evidence: The attempt-7 demo contained SaaS-specific action tables, route switches, Definition filtering, sample data, application chrome, and product styling.
The attempt-7 Experience declared no actors or tasks while its unit cited publicRespondent and four task ids.
Attempt 7 authored no Needs Document and no direct rendered-Need trace.
The attempt-7 report omitted surface-local, authorization-boundary, and unsupported phases.
The attempt-7 host filtered one Definition into setup and public-response forms, changing form membership outside the Definition.

represented_areas: Account access, onboarding, environment, and team
Forms, publishing, preview, and public completion
Explicit LIVE, ASSISTED, PREVIEW, and DISABLED feature posture
Connected, scoped, hidden, and parameterized navigation
Structured Definitions, Experience, Response Actions, Registry, and Data Sources
remaining_limitations: The corrected artifacts are a structured reconstruction, not a fresh blind public-builder replay.
The technical evidence does not become human product approval; the aggregate demo claim remains held until approval is explicit.

This assessment does not establish persistence, tenant isolation, authentication or recovery, billing execution, entitlement enforcement, external delivery, production verification behavior, release, or deployment.
